title: SeisMark: A Large-Scale Open Benchmark for Robust 3D Seismic Fault Detection
claim: A staged procedure combining procedural generation, physics simulation, and learned style transfer yields realistic data while preserving ground-truth labels.
layout: 3 stage boxes left-to-right, 3D cube outputs below, dashed enclosure
description: Three colored rounded boxes run left to right across the top, linked by gray arrows. They are 1. Procedural Model Builder (blue), 2. Forward Modeling (orange) and 3. Diffusion-based Style Transfer (teal). Each box has a short description, such as Perlin/fractal noise heterogeneity or basin-specific Australia/North Sea. Gray arrows drop from each box to 3D seismic cube renderings in a dashed purple enclosure. The cubes, left to right, are a colorful velocity volume, a purple cube with yellow fault lines, a grayscale pseudo-seismic cube, and a styled realistic seismic cube. Colored labels sit under the cubes. A bottom caption reads 'Ground-truth fault labels preserved through pipeline' between double-headed arrows. The eye goes first to the top stage boxes, then to the cubes.
caption: Synthetic seismic data generation pipeline. Stage 1 builds procedural 3D velocity models with accompanying ground-truth fault
abstract: We introduce SeisMark, a large-scale open benchmark designed to bridge the gap between verifiable ground truth and realistic texture in 3D seismic fault detection. Using a novel pipeline merging procedural geology with diffusion-based synthesis, we produce domain-realistic (survey-specific) textured volumes that expose significant brittleness in existing models masked by simplified physics data. Experiments demonstrate that SeisMark acts as a rigorous discriminator, distinguishing robust modern architecture from legacy model that suffers performance collapse under realistic domain shifts. We release this benchmark to the community to serve as a verifiable standard for developing trustworthy, deployment-ready AI for safety-critical subsurface applications.
